course_details.Overview of class: This course is part of the full-year sequence that aims to help you become familiar with the processes and possibilities involved in piano teaching. Winter quarter will focus on various teaching approaches, strategies, and appropriate materials for teaching beginners beyond the first years of lessons. A combination of lectures, discussions, observations, and supervised teaching will help you develop effective and sophisticated teaching skills.
course_details.Registration Requirements: Students must be undergraduate music majors who have completed their core curriculum. Please contact the instructor (lam.wong@northwestern.edu) to receive recommendations on registering for the course.
course_details.Learning Objectives: Explore various method books and teaching materials tailored for piano study beyond the first years of lessons; Evaluate the effectiveness of creative and conventional technical drills; Review the "Classics" repertoire for piano studies; Address the processes and challenges for transfer students.
course_details.Teaching Method: Attendance and participation in Tuesday seminars are required, in addition to assigned observation and teaching duties.
course_details.Evaluation Method: Students will be evaluated for their success in assisting and teaching in assigned children's lessons, assigned projects and observations, contributions to seminar discussions, and a final project.
course_details.Class Materials (Required): Students should be collegiate members of Music Teachers National Association (MTNA). The membership fee is $36 (subject to a small adjustment for 2025-26) for the entire academic year.
course_details.Class Materials (Suggested):
1. Music for Millions Series
2. Keith Snell Piano Series
3. Sight Reading Series by Bastien Piano Library
4. A Line a Day Sight Reading Series
5. Improve Your Sight-reading! Series
course_details.Class Notes: It is recommended to register for this course for the full-year sequence. Attendance at the first class is mandatory.

This course prepares master students to become successful piano teachers within the music community. It includes regular observations, pedagogy projects, and community engagement with the Northwestern Music Academy and local Music Teachers Association. The curriculum covers a comprehensive approach to piano instruction and technical training methods. Students will also learn about community music schools, standardized tests, and professional engagement.
course_details.Registration Requirements: Students must be graduate music majors. Please contact the instructor (lam.wong@northwestern.edu) to receive recommendations on registering for the course.
course_details.Learning Objectives: This course prepares students to become successful music teachers by equipping them with comprehensive piano instruction techniques, strategies for supporting intermediate students, insights into running community music schools, and skills for engaging with professional associations and creating online enrichment programs.
course_details.Teaching Method: Attendance and participation in Friday seminars are required, in addition to assigned observation and various projects outside of class time.
course_details.Evaluation Method: Students will be evaluated for their level of success in weekly written assignments, regular observations, class presentations, and pedagogy projects.
course_details.Class Materials (Suggested):
1. Piano Method books from Faber & Faber series
2. Piano Method Books from Hal Leonard Piano Library
3. Piano Method Books from The Music Tree
4. Piano Method Books from John Thompson's Easiest Piano Course
5. Piano Method Books from Music for Piano
6. Music for Millions Series
7. Keith Snell Piano Series
course_details.Class Notes: Attendance at the first class is mandatory.
